_doc: One corpus for every reader of PR, comment and commit text (vws-deploy#439 AC2 class 2). Each case: the raw text and the visible text a reader must see (trailing newlines ignored). guard-agents.sh visible_text and orchestrate.py visible_text must both return 'visible'.

cases.name: plain text is unchanged
a lone carriage return inside a line is content
cases.source: pass: only a CRLF line end is a line end; Rule D's ^ does not start a line after a lone CR

cases.name: multi-line HTML comment hides every line inside it
cases.source: vws-deploy#430 review 5629555715: comments were removed only within one line

cases.name: HTML comment closed on the next line hides the evidence
two comments on one line
an unclosed comment runs to the end
a comment opener inside a fence is code
a fence inside a comment is hidden
a shorter fence does not close a longer one
cases.source: guard P2 (Match closing fences to the opening delimiter, 6 repo copies)

cases.name: a tilde line does not close a backtick fence
cases.source: guard P2 (Match closing fences to the opening delimiter)

cases.name: a fence line with text after it does not close
cases.source: CommonMark: a closing fence has no info string

cases.name: an unclosed fence runs to the end
a longer run closes the fence
a fence with an info string
a fence indented with spaces and a tab
CRLF line ends are read as LF
cases.source: PR bodies saved in a browser use CRLF; the Python reader kept the fence open to the end and the awk reader kept the CR

cases.name: a form feed is not indentation
cases.source: CommonMark indentation is spaces and tabs; the awk reader opened a fence here and hid the line

cases.name: a vertical tab before a closing fence does not close it
cases.source: the awk reader closed the fence on [[:space:]] and showed the line

cases.name: an Agent line in a fence is an example
an Agent line in a comment is hidden
